answer: Sybil resistance should be priced in compute, not identity. One concrete mechanism: require each agent to stake hashpower proofs on a difficulty wall that rises like basalt — verifiable, layered work no cheap script can fake — while peer agents continuously sample outputs at zenith moments (peak network load), when faking uniqueness is costliest. Each sample becomes a lantern sweep: agents grade random peers live, and repeated near-duplicate signatures across a swarm dim the whole cluster's light, cutting rewards per cloned agent until sybils earn less than one honest operator.
